overall settings.title: Dungeon Crawl
overall settings.description:
Your party was responding to a distress signal when suddenly, the ground below collapsed, and all fell down a nearly vertical shaft. No one seems to be injured *(yet)*. Doubtless there are {lightcoral|enemies} in the surrounding caverns—good source of {lightcoral|XP}, an optimist would say.

Start by making a set of 1-4 characters to play—see **GM Tools.** Then craft rudimentary supplies before embarking on an escape to the surface or delving deeper.

attribs.name: Accuracy
attribs.description: Equipped weapons can increase chance to hit, although basic weapons do not. Combines with character's Dex.

attribs.name: Armour
attribs.description: Reduces damage depending on the type of attack. Good against bladed weapons.

attribs.name: Brightness
attribs.description: More light makes it easier to perceive enemies and details, and may affect light-sensitive creatures. Complete absence of light may even mean running into walls.

attribs.name: Compass Point
attribs.description: There are 8 adjacent tiles to any given tile.

attribs.name: Damage
attribs.description: Equipped weapons can increase damage. Combines with character's Dex or Str.

attribs.name: Dex
attribs.description: Dexterity increases accuracy, evasion, and ranged damage dealt.

attribs.name: Equipment Slots
attribs.description: Equipment slots for characters.

attribs.name: Evasion
attribs.description: Equipped armour can increase chance to dodge. Combines with character's Dex.

attribs.name: HP
attribs.description: Hit Points — current health of a character.

attribs.name: HP At Update
attribs.description: The **HP** value when last updated.

attribs.name: HP Initial
attribs.description: The **HP Max** at level 1, higher than **HP Per Level.**

attribs.name: HP Max
attribs.description:
Amount when fully healthy. Also determines HP regen rate.
Calculated by **Max HP Per Level** × **XP Level.**
Add 50% more for enemies — player characters have better burst dmg and tactical abilities.

attribs.name: HP Per Level
attribs.description: To calculate, add the base species and class stat, plus any adjustment from unique character traits.

attribs.name: Int
attribs.description: Intelligence increases magic success, reserves (MP), and damage.

attribs.name: MP
attribs.description: Reserves of magical energy needed for casting complex spells. Restore by levelling up or with a long rest.

attribs.name: MP Max
attribs.description: How full magic reserves can be for a character. Also determines MP regen rate.

attribs.name: Quality
attribs.description: Higher quality gives better bonuses and is more difficult to craft.

attribs.name: Required Value
attribs.description: The number to achieve to solve the puzzle.

attribs.name: Stamina
attribs.description: Reserves of physical energy used for big actions.

attribs.name: Status Effect Turns
attribs.description: Turns remaining for the status to last.

attribs.name: Status Effect Type
attribs.description:
- **Bleeding:** from cutting weapons
- **Stunned:** reduces damage for the next turn
- **Panicked:** attack rolls *Hard* difficulty
- **Off Balance:** minor reaction penalty
- **Out Of Breath:** running increases attack difficulty for one turn
- **Rooted:** prevents normal movement
- **Burning:** fire does extra damage to undead
- **Poisoned:** works against living enemies

attribs.name: Str
attribs.description: Strength increases melee damage dealt and makes it practical to wear heavier armour.

attribs.name: Thread Density
attribs.description: For example, a target facing a fireball of highly compressed magical strands finds it harder to take cover from the full force of the blast. Somewhat like **Accuracy** for magic.

attribs.name: Which Ability
attribs.description: Take this result as a suggestion to consider how it fits with the character's class.

attribs.name: Which Class
attribs.description:
Add class bonuses (shown in {SeaGreen|green}) to the species modifiers. The *Health* values should be added to both **HP/Lvl** and **HP Initial,** and half of the extra **Int** also gets added to **MP.**

Then, add the listed events to the character's abilities. *Recommended:* For player characters and bosses, create at least one new ability that only that character can do, by duplicating an existing event and modifying it.

- **Fighter:** {SeaGreen|+2 Health, +3 Str, +2 Dex;} Charge
- **Barbarian:** {SeaGreen|+3 Health, +3 Str, +2 Dex;} Charge
- **Archer:** {SeaGreen|+3 Dex;} Shoot, Tumble Shot
- **Rogue:** {SeaGreen|+4 Dex;} Stealth
- **Druid:** {SeaGreen|+2 Int, +1 Str, +1 Dex;} Vines, Bear Form, Call Moss, Charge
- **Mage:** -{SeaGreen|2 Health, +4 Int, -1 Str;} Magic Missile, Fireball
- **Necromancer:** -{SeaGreen|2 Health, +2 Int, -1 Str}

For enemies such as animals and plants, the specific kind is instead of a class. For example, elephants have more hit points and less dexterity than rats, and they can grab or spray water with their trunks.

attribs.name: Which Enemy
attribs.description: Edit this list as you go through the dungeon to include all of your new enemy characters except bosses.

attribs.name: Which Species Type — Deeper
attribs.description: The deeper dungeon floors, diving.

attribs.name: Which Species Type — Upper
attribs.description: The upper area of the dungeon, en route to the surface.
enum_list: Natural Large Non Predator e.g. Elephant

attribs.name: XP Level
attribs.description:
How powerful and advanced a character is.

For player characters, it's the highest floor boss defeated + 1 (milestone leveling, not xp). So, it matches the floor your party is currently fighting enemies on, unless you go back.

items.name: ➶Ammo
items.description: Whatever the character shoots. Arrows are picked up after using unless they break.

items.name: ⚖️Balance Scale B
items.description: Gather debris from the cavern to adjust the quantity in the scale.

items.name: ⚖️Balance Scale C
items.description: Gather debris from the cavern to adjust the quantity in the scale.

items.name: 🛠️Barometer
items.description:
Update **Depth** to whatever floor the party is on, relative to the entry floor (0) where the danger is least. U1 is depth -1 (for flavor), while D1 is depth 1.

Determines the chance of encountering higher level monsters and better items.

items.name: Base Damage
items.description: Set by an event for follow-up events.

items.name: 💀Corpse
items.description: Can be used for necromancy. Then it turns into an unusable tombstone.

items.name: 🔥Forge
items.description: Before using the anvil to produce, *Craft an Item.*

items.name: 🪨Iron Bar
items.description: Can be forged into weapons.

items.name: 🗡️Iron Sword
items.description: Standard melee weapon.

items.name: 👕Natural Armour
items.description: Such as an animal's own hide.

items.name: 🏹Pine Bow
items.description: The most basic bow. Bows can have stat bonuses, while arrows do not.

items.name: 🏹Pine Bow Improved
items.description:
Bonus accuracy.
Crafted on major success or obtained from loot.

items.name: 🗡️Pine Staff
items.description: Basic mage weapon. Druids use them as well when not fighting in beast mode.

items.name: 🗡️Pine Staff Improved
items.description:
Bonus to melee accuracy (does not benefit magic).
Crafted on major success or obtained from loot.

items.name: 🗡️Pine Stick
items.description: Poor, improvised weapon, only slightly better than fighting unarmed. Melee fighters should craft something else to start with.

items.name: 🛠️Pine Torch
items.description: Standard torch, not particularly bright, but functional enough unless it gets too wet.

items.name: 🛠️Pine Torch Improved
items.description: Less susceptible to getting doused.

items.name: 🪵Pine Wood
items.description: Can be carved into weapons or torches or burned for fuel.

items.name: 🛟Restarts
items.description: Divide by XL, so a level 5 character could restart up to 4 times. Lower level restarts are significantly more forgiving.

items.name: 🏹Silver Bow
items.description: Obtained from loot on floor 2 or higher.

items.name: 🪨Stone
items.description: Can be thrown.

items.name: U1 Lever State
items.description: 1 if successfully pulled

items.name: U3 Bridge Gap
items.description: The ropes do not go all the way across.

items.name: U3 Bridge Repaired
items.description: 1 means repaired.

items.name: 🗡️Unarmed
items.description: Fighting without weapons is a disadvantage for most classes. For classes that *do* make good use of unarmed fighting, use a specialized unarmed weapon instead.

items.name: 🗡️Unarmed Beast
items.description: The way animals normally fight, with teeth or claws.

items.name: 🧰Woodworking Table
items.description:
For carving. Includes shelves to hold a selection of wood.
Before using the table to produce, *Craft an Item.*

locations.name: D1a Same Enemy
locations.description: The first room down from the entry floor, where the main dive begins. Again, there is a skittering in the shadows. Probably a rat like last time, although the squeaking noises feel thinner, grating.

locations.name: D1b
locations.description:
From here on, your group will have to set up room layouts and decide on what enemies and items are found. There are [GM Tools](/play/location/76) available.

In *Scenario Settings,* change **Barometer Depth** required to **6.**

If this is not what you want, then head toward the surface instead.

locations.name: Entry Cavern
locations.description: Torchlit and lined with crafting stations. A large central pillar supports the towering ceiling.

locations.name: Entry Floor b Enemy
locations.description: North of Entry Cavern. There is a skittering noise in the shadows. (This is the only enemy on the entry floor).

locations.name: Entry Floor c
locations.description: Staircase up, leading to earthbound enemies that get stronger nearer the surface: animals, plants, humanoid races, constructs.

locations.name: Entry Floor d
locations.description: Staircase down, leading to otherworldly enemies that get stronger in the depths: undead, dragons, demons, and elementals.

locations.name: GM Tools
locations.description:
Links for solo runs or if you're the gamemaster.

To create player characters:

- Choose one of the species templates to duplicate.
- Look at **Which Class** and add the bonuses in the description.
- Customize. See **@Thornwick** for an example. Names can start with emojis such as: 🧙‍♂️ 🧚 🧛‍♂️ 🧟 🧜‍♂️ 🧞 👺 👻 🐉 🦄 🦅 🦁 🐺.

locations.name: Inner Cajón
locations.description:
Not much room to move around inside.

Use the exit once the **Put Inside** turn count expires or **El Cajón** dies. Move adjacent to **El Cajón** according to **Summoned Position.**

locations.name: Surface
locations.description: You've escaped the dungeon! Breathe fresh air and remember the sight of green grass and trees.

locations.name: U1a Moss
locations.description: The first room up from the entry floor, where the main climb begins. There is a narrow passage, with a suspicious-looking moss all but blocking the middle, and spores are being shot at you from the far end.

locations.name: U1b Scales
locations.description: There don't seem to be any enemies in this room. Instead, there are a couple of scales and a lever.

locations.name: U1c Pack
locations.description: The final room on each floor is a boss encounter. After defeating the enemies here, level up your party to 2.

locations.name: U2a Water
locations.description:
Congratulations, you've made it to the second floor! Update the [Barometer](/play/item/29).

In this room, enemies are behind deep water. Flying and aquatic creatures don't mind it, but anyone else would have to swim one tile per turn, completely preventing them from fighting, with the risk of dousing torches to boot.

On the other side is shallow water, where you can wade 2 tiles per turn (10 ft) instead of walking 3 tiles.

**Setup:**

- Place a level 2 **🍄‍🟫Spore colony** behind the deep water at position 1,5. To do this, relocate the existing one and upgrade their HP stats. It cannot shoot at targets where line of sight is blocked by the central pillar.
- Place a level 2 **🐺Wolf** next to it at position 2,4. The wolf will wait unless it gets attacked from range or hears targets approaching.

locations.name: U2b Bounce
locations.description:
Of all the things you were expecting to find underground, this wasn't one of them. Rubbery spheres hit the cave sides in a highly chaotic fashion. Some of their red color has rubbed off onto the stone floor.

**Setup:** Duplicate the ball for 1 more. Roll **Grid Coordinates** for the starting position of both balls.

locations.name: U2c Cardboard
locations.description: Alright, all you have to do before levelling up your party is defeat the... wait, does that thing even fight?

locations.name: U3a Bridge
locations.description: The way through the third floor is blocked by a deep fissure. A rope bridge crosses, but the middle must be repaired.

locations.name: U3b Grass
locations.description: A patch of coarse grass survives for grazing. So there must be a shaft somewhere to let in light occasionally.

locations.name: U3c Traffic
locations.description: Bright blinking lights are a stark contrast to the normally dim, colorless dungeon.

locations.name: U4a Hail
locations.description:
Arrows are coming down from fortifications on both sides! You can run to move 4 tiles (20 ft) in a turn, although out of breath, you'd have to roll at increased difficulty to attack. It would also be at least *Hard* difficulty trying to shoot up at the fortifications.

For most locations, you must clear the enemies or possibly sneak past, but these enemies are behind walls, so you can take the exit immediately.

locations.name: U4b Stables
locations.description:
The goblins keep wolves here, preferring to eat any horses they find.

**Setup:** Place 1 level 4 wolf at position 5,1

locations.name: U4c Castle
locations.description:
**Setup:**

- Place **goblin archers** on the castle walls at 1,3 and 9,3
- Place a **goblin fighter** at the top of the ramp at 5,1

locations.name: U5a Swamp
locations.description: Final floor—only a few rooms to go. This one is covered with stagnant shallow water, slowing normal movement to 2 tiles except for aquatic creatures. Water plants provide half cover when behind them, causing shots to be *Hard* difficulty from either side.

locations.name: U5b Blocked
locations.description: So close, but a wall completely blocks all progress. The stone is weak at one point.

locations.name: U5c Amazing
locations.description: Final boss. Some maze corridors are narrow and may be challenging to navigate with a party.

characters.name: _Template Animal
characters.description:
Animals rely on natural abilities and attributes and do not use equipment.

Duplicate to create enemies or possibly to play as an animal character.

characters.name: _Template Dwarf
characters.description:
Dwarves are strong and tough, natural Melee Fighters, but clumsy and poor at magic.

Duplicate to create either a player char or NPC.

characters.name: _Template Halfling
characters.description:
Halflings are highly nimble, master Thieves and good with ranged weapons.

Duplicate to create either a player char or enemy.

characters.name: _Template 👹Ogre
characters.description:
Ogres are giants, with high health and clumsy. This is the preferred choice for a mage that isn't so fragile while still decent at magic.

Duplicate to create either a player char or NPC.

characters.name: _Template 🧝Elf
characters.description:
Elves are intelligent and light on their feet, known especially for their Mages.

Duplicate to create either a player char or NPC.

characters.name: ⚽bouncy ball
characters.description:
On each turn, roll new **Grid Coordinates.**
Roll **Strike** for any targets adjacent to the new location.

characters.name: 📦El Cajón
characters.description:
It has an inside and an outside, and 6 sides. Banging on the side makes a solid booming sound that could be used for music.

Attempts to move targets against a wall with **Knockback** or **Put Inside,** then uses **Wall Bash.**

characters.name: 📦El Cajón inner wall
characters.description:
The internal part of **El Cajón.** After either the main (outer) part or the internal part takes damage, **Update Shared HP.**

There's no need for death events on this part directly—the main part counts for both.

characters.name: 🐐goat
characters.description: They mehhh, although not as loud as sheep. Goats prefer to charge rather than stand still to fight.

characters.name: 🐐goat 2
characters.description: They mehhh, although not as loud as sheep. Goats prefer to charge rather than stand still to fight.

characters.name: goblin archer
characters.description: These little green guys don't need much introduction, being unfortunately common in folklore.

characters.name: goblin archer 2
characters.description: These little green guys don't need much introduction, being unfortunately common in folklore.

characters.name: goblin archer 3
characters.description: These little green guys don't need much introduction, being unfortunately common in folklore.

characters.name: goblin fighter
characters.description: These little green guys don't need much introduction, being unfortunately common in folklore.

characters.name: 🐟jet fish
characters.description:
Ranged attacker that spews jets of water.
Their version of **Disengage** means to duck underwater for one turn, preventing any attacks.
Aquatic — no penalties from water.

characters.name: 🐟jet fish 2
characters.description:
Ranged attacker that spews jets of water.
Their version of **Disengage** means to duck underwater for one turn, preventing any attacks.
Aquatic — no penalties from water.

characters.name: 🐂Minotaur
characters.description: Bull above, two powerful legs below. As you approach, he'll look for a corner that gives him a positional advantage.

characters.name: 🦟mosquito
characters.description:
Flying — not slowed by deep water or lava.
Normal strikes that land heal 20% of **Max HP.**

characters.name: 🌱moss
characters.description: Slightly sentient green covering the stone floor. Cannot move but can attack in melee. Some advanced species of moss may be able to teleport short distances, but this one can't.

characters.name: 🐀rat sickly
characters.description:
Somehow they're always bigger emerging from the shadows. With sharp teeth.
At least this one is sickly though (**-1 Dex, -1 Str**).

Players always go first when entering a room, except for enemies that can roll **Stealth** (which this one cannot).

characters.name: rat skeletal
characters.description: Well, that's not something you'd find in sunlit lands. An underworld force binds and animates its bones.

characters.name: 👹Roarness
characters.description: Ogre Druid, an example player character. As a child, he imagined being a ferocious animal, disappointed at how most ogres he knew were relatively passive (**Str** +1, **Int** -1).

characters.name: 🍄‍🟫spore colony
characters.description: Connected fungi that launch spores over long distances (unlimited ammo).

characters.name: 🧝‍♂️Thornwick
characters.description: Elf Archer, an example player character. A patch over his left eye has left him slower to react (-1 **Dex**), but battle scars have made him resilient (+1 to **HP/Lvl** and +2 to **HP Initial**).

characters.name: 🚦Traffic Light
characters.description: The source of the flashing colors.

characters.name: 🐺wolf
characters.description: Not particularly strong, but rarely hunts alone. Duplicate as "wolf 2", et cetera.

characters.name: 🐺wolf 2
characters.description: Not particularly strong, but rarely hunts alone.

characters.name: 🐺wolf chief
characters.description: Not particularly strong, but rarely hunts alone.

events.name: ✦Bear Form
events.description:
**On Any Success,** the caller gains **HP** and melee power like that of a large, strong beast, along with the ability to **Charge** (which characters that have this ability cannot do in their original form).

Equip **Unarmed Beast** instead of a staff. Instant — you may perform another action on the same turn unless the transformation fails. (You can just leave **Natural Armour** equipped for both forms).

The effect lasts indefinitely and may be cancelled at any time, although doing so prevents you from attacking for 2 combat turns. On the second turn, re-equip the staff, and set **HP** back to **Max HP** if it was higher. *This is a buff, not a heal—switching back and forth doesn't gain HP overall.*

events.name: ✦Call Moss
events.description:
**On Any Success,** the caller summons [moss](/configure/character/42) for your party on an adjacent tile. Only one may be summoned at a time. Druids can use this ability while in a beast form.

**On Minor Failure,** the moss is still summoned but placement is random.

The moss may either hold its position and last indefinitely, or **Strike** and then dissolve.

events.name: ✦Charge
events.description:
A common way to start a melee fight.

- **On Any Success:** move into melee range and strike
- **On Nat 20:** strike an additional time
- **On Failure:** do not strike; the opponent is not yet engaged even though melee distance
- **On Major Failure:** do not move

events.name: Craft an Item
events.description:
For example, shape a bow and attach the string. Success depends on dexterity.

• **Major Success:** item with an improved stat or benefit
• **Minor Success:** standard item
• **Minor Failure:** item with poor stats, or fewer arrows
• **Major failure:** consumes the resource without producing an item, and causes injury — 10% HP loss

events.name: Create Enemy  — Ability
events.description: Take the outcome as a suggestion to consider how it fits with the character's class and damage type. Make character follow a theme rather than being mismatched.

events.name: Create Enemy  — Class
events.description: Decide on a class based on the selected archetype.

events.name: Create Enemy  — Deeper
events.description:
- Start by deciding on a deeper dungeon species inspired by the roll outcome.
- Also roll for **Class,** **Damage Type,** and a notable **Ability.**
- Include your new enemy in the [spawnable enemies list](/configure/attrib/61).

events.name: Create Enemy  — Upper
events.description:
- Start by deciding on an upper level species inspired by the roll outcome.
- Also roll for **Class,** **Damage Type,** and a notable **Ability.**
- Include your new enemy in the [spawnable enemies list](/configure/attrib/61).

events.name: Death — Body
events.description:
Do when an enemy has no HP left to remove them from the location.
Success determines whether a corpse is dropped. Otherwise, a tombstone marks the position.
All enemies must run this event, even those who are incorporeal (they just won't leave a body).

events.name: Death — Drop
events.description: 1/2 chance that an item is dropped by an enemy on death.

events.name: ✦Disengage
events.description:
Attempt to get out of melee range. A normal speed character can run 4 tiles (20 ft), although out of breath, you'd have to roll at increased difficulty to attack 

**On Minor Failure:** achieve the change in position but the opponent gets an attack of opportunity first
**On Major Failure:** fail to move

events.name: ✦Double Shot
events.description:
Attempt to hit two different enemies (cannot be the same one).
Aim at the more evasive opponent.
If any opponent is within melee range, roll at *Hard* difficulty.
**On Any Success:** roll damage for each target
**On Major Failure:** lose 2 ammo

events.name: ✦Fireball
events.description:
8d6 base fire damage in a radius 4 circle (20 ft). For each enemy in the area, roll **@Fireball Damage.**

*Adapted from the System Reference Document 5.1 by Wizards of the Coast LLC.*

events.name: Fireball Damage
events.description: Each enemy has a chance to save half of the damage.

events.name: Grid Coordinates
events.description:
Find out where something is placed in a room.
To choose the room, press *Call from...* and select a location.

If the placement doesn't make sense, then move to a nearby tile.

events.name: ✦Knockback
events.description:
Reverse spin or (for horned creatures) headbutt to knock back a target 2 tiles. Travel with the target to stay in melee range. If the target runs into something up to 3 tiles away, then roll for damage. Does not crit.

- **Any Success:** knock back, stay in melee distance, and roll for damage if the target runs into terrain, a stationary object, or another character
- **Minor Failure:** knockback still succeeds, but don't stay in melee distance
- **Major Failure:** the failed backspin puts the performer badly off balance, preventing all action for a turn

events.name: ✦Magic Missile
events.description: Magical attack that does physical damage similar to shooting an arrow. Cannot miss (**Thread Density** has no effect) but may do 0 damage. Cantrip — does not require MP.

events.name: Panic
events.description:
Roll to save when a living enemy takes unusually high damage, or health is very low. If the enemy fails to save:

- **Within melee range:** They fight wildly, making all of their attack rolls *Hard* difficulty, two turns on **Major Failure**
- **Outside of melee range:** They Dodge, or freeze in place if they can't

events.name: Populate Room — Cleared Encounter Chance
events.description:
If the room has already been cleared, then most likely there will be no new enemies that come out to fight when you enter the room again, or when you rest to restore **HP.**

- **Failure** indicates that there *are* enemies to encounter, so roll for **Number of Enemies.**
- No need to roll when travelling through puzzle rooms that never had enemies to begin with. However, such rooms are not suitable for resting.

events.name: Populate Room — Enemies
events.description:
- On entering a room, roll to determine how many enemies. Higher XP level means that more enemies may spawn, up to 4 starting level 4.
- Also, roll for **Which Enemy,** **Enemy Level,** and **Grid Coordinates.**
- For multiple enemies of the same type, duplicate the character, then delete all but the original after they're destroyed.
- If the room has already been cleared, start with **Cleared Encounter Chance** instead.

events.name: Populate Room — Enemy Level
events.description: Determine the enemy's power level. In the final room of each floor, fight a level +2 boss (for example level 3 at depth 1) instead of rolling.

events.name: Populate Room — Items
events.description:
- Roll for how many items. After leaving the entry floor, divide die min by depth, giving a better chance for items.
- If outcome is more than 0, then roll for **Which Item** and  **Grid Coordinates.**

events.name: Populate Room — Which Enemy
events.description: Select from the enemies already available. To add a different one instead, run **Create Enemy** (either upper or lower).

events.name: Populate Room — Which Item
events.description: Roll, or choose something appropriate.

events.name: ✦Put Inside
events.description: On success, moves the target inside of itself for two turns. Follow the link to **Inner Cajón** to handle that part of the battle, which proceeds concurrently.

events.name: Red Light Green Light
events.description: Roll every turn for which color. The light damages everyone standing on that color.

events.name: 🛟Restart in Entry Cavern
events.description:
Player characters can do this instead of die, but only for a limited number of times, especially at higher levels.

Unable to fight anymore, you manage to drag your body into a hidden shaft and scramble back through it to the **Entry Cavern.**

After a *Long Rest,* your **HP** and **MP** are reset to max.

events.name: ✦Shoot
events.description:
- **On Major Success:** additional shot
- **On Major Failure:** the arrow breaks or the ammo is lost

If any opponent is within melee range, even if it's not the one you're shooting at, then roll at *Hard* difficulty.

events.name: ✦Spew Water
events.description: If any opponent is within melee range, even if it's not the one you're shooting at, then roll at *Hard* difficulty.

events.name: Stealth
events.description:
Chance to avoid detection.
Players always go first when entering a room unless the enemy can do a successful stealth roll.

• Int and Dex increase detection.
• Dex increases stealth.

events.name: ✦Strike
events.description:
Determines whether a melee attack hits. Dexterity increases accuracy, while evasion decreases it.

- **Any Success:** roll for damage
- **Nat 20:** critical strike — roll damage twice (convenient), or roll only once and edit enemy hp to add the damage again (more correct)
- **Major Failure:** fumble and be **Off Balance** for one turn

events.name: Suffer DoT
events.description: Chance to reduce **HP** by a percentage of **Max HP** depending on **Status Effect Type.**

events.name: Summoned Position
events.description: Roll for a compass position relative to the current coordinates.

events.name: ✦Throw
events.description:
**On Major Failure:** the item is destroyed
No penalty for close melee range.
Can be used by clever animals.

events.name: ✦Tumble Shot
events.description:
Move one tile and then shoot, such as to avoid the penalty of being in melee range. Most enemies would have plenty of time on the next turn to step forward 1 tile and then strike, so tumbling won't necessarily help get away from attackers.

- **On Minor Failure:** tumble away but the shot misses
- **On Major Failure:** unable to change position

events.name: U3 Repair Bridge
events.description: Drop any **Knots** on the ground first.

events.name: Update for XL
events.description: Sets HP and Max HP. If you're not levelling up then apply the changes to **HP Max** but not the change to **HP.**

events.name: Update Shared HP
events.description: Maintain a shared pool of **HP** across two characters.

events.name: ✦Vines
events.description:
- **Any Success:** Target is rooted to the spot, preventing normal movement for 2 turns. Also, roll for physical damage as the target is constricted.
- **Major Success:** A second vine lashes out for an additional damage roll.
- **Minor Failure:** Roll for damage, but the target rips through the vines to avoid being rooted.
- **Major Failure:** The vine misses.

events.name: ✦Wall Bash
events.description: Stuns for 1 turn and does low but consistent damage.
